panels.title: Faithfulness (offline)
panels.description: M2 is measured offline over a fixed 100-alert sample, not streamed per alert, so it has no time series to plot here.

options.content:
**M2 is measured, offline.** Entity preservation 0.96 · corruption-free 1.00 · hallucination lower bound 0.000 · example echo 0.68 · 41 distinct explanations per 100 alerts.

These come from a batch run over a fixed 100-alert sample (`reports/llm_faithfulness_metrics.csv`), not from the live stream, so there is no series to chart. A zero here describes the mechanical checks, not correctness.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alerts")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "soc_alert" and contains(value: r._field, set: ["risk_score", "response_ms"]))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.alert_id and exists r.source_ip and exists r.dst_port)
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time", "alert_id", "source_ip", "dst_port", "priority", "anomaly_type", "mitre_tactic"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "priority", "source_ip", "dst_port", "risk_score", "anomaly_type", "mitre_tactic", "response_ms", "alert_id"])
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 10)

panels.title: MTTD Timeline
panels.description: Mean time to detect per alert: detected_at minus ingested_at. The architecture called for this panel and it could not be built, because mttd_ms was computed on every record and then dropped before the InfluxDB write. Both timestamps are flow-relative, so on replayed CICIDS-2017 the points sit at the 2017 capture time -- set the dashboard range to the capture window, not to a recent one.

from(bucket: "alerts")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "soc_alert" and r._field == "mttd_ms")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.model_used == "random_forest")
  |> group()
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)

from(bucket: "alerts")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)

  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.model_used == "if_ae_fallback")
  |> group()
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)

panels.title: Alerts By Deciding Branch
panels.description: Which half of the cascade decided each alert. On in-distribution traffic random_forest decides about 99.8% of rows; on the out-of-distribution synthetic overlay the fallback decided 100%. A shift toward if_ae_fallback means RF is abstaining, which is the signal worth watching.

panels.title: Enrichment Latency By Provenance
panels.description: Per-event cost of src/services/enrich.py, split by where the answer came from. An uncached OpenCTI lookup measured ~2,157 ms mean against ~0.055 ms for a cache hit, so the cache is not an optimisation here, it is what makes the stage viable. Read against the 0.023 ms scoring decision: enrichment is not on the detection path, and this panel is why it must not be.

panels.title: IoC Match Rate
panels.description: Share of enriched events where an observable matched a pattern-verified indicator. Expect this to be low and do not read it as a fault: a sample of ~3,000 of this OpenCTI instance's 55,219 indicators held exactly 2 with an ipv4-addr pattern, because its connectors publish hashes, URLs and domains. Flow records offer IPs, so there is very little to match.

targets.query:
matched = from(bucket: "alerts")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "soc_enrich" and r._field == "latency_ms" and r.matched == "true")
  |> group() |> count()
total = from(bucket: "alerts")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "soc_enrich" and r._field == "latency_ms")
  |> group() |> count()
join(tables: {m: matched, t: total}, on: ["_start"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._start, _value: float(v: r._value_m) / float(v: r._value_t)}))
